architecture: custom CNN trained from scratch (4x [Conv2D-BatchNorm-MaxPool] with 16/32/64/128 filters, GlobalAveragePooling2D, Dense(64, relu), Dropout(0.4), Dense(1, sigmoid)); input 128x128x3, Rescaling(1/255) and light augmentation (RandomFlip, RandomRotation 0.05, RandomZoom 0.1, RandomContrast 0.1) built into the model graph
why_not_mobilenetv2_or_pretrained_weight: This environment still cannot reach storage.googleapis.com, huggingface.co or kaggle.com (all return HTTP 403 from the network proxy), so ImageNet-pretrained weights remain unavailable, exactly as documented in app/classifier/inference.py for the original 6-class MobileNetV2(weights=None) build. Unlike the previous development session, this one COULD reach github.com/raw.githubusercontent.com/codeload.github.com, which is how the real dataset below was obtained. A smaller from-scratch architecture was used instead of the full MobileNetV2 purely so training would converge in a practical amount of time on CPU with no pretrained features to start from.

dataset.source: garythung/trashnet (the dataset released with Thung & Yang, Stanford CS229, 2016), obtained via a public GitHub mirror that commits the resized JPEGs directly: https://github.com/winkhai/trash-recycling-classifier
dataset.note: This is the same TrashNet dataset already cited in the project's literature/methodology chapters, not a new/different dataset.
dataset.split_integrity: train/valid/test folders were provided pre-split by the dataset mirror and were kept separate throughout -- test images were never seen during training or model selection, so the test metrics below are a genuine held-out evaluation, not a training-set score.

training.class_weight: inverse-frequency weighting applied (paper images are ~23% of the data) so the model is not just rewarded for guessing the majority class

honest_interpretation: Overall accuracy (90.1%) clears this project's own evaluation gate (>=85%, see ModelVersion.meets_evaluation_gate) and beats the naive always-predict-not_paper baseline (76.5%) by a meaningful margin, so the model is genuinely detecting something about paper rather than exploiting class imbalance. However, recall on paper is the real weak point: only 62% of actual paper items in the test set were correctly flagged as paper (34 of 90 were missed and fell through as not_paper). Precision is high (93%) -- when the model does say 'paper', it is usually right. In plain terms: it will under-call paper more often than it will falsely call something paper. This is disclosed here and in the app rather than only reporting the headline accuracy figure.
scope: This model answers one question only: is this item paper or not? It does not yet distinguish plastic, metal, glass or organic from each other -- those all currently fall under 'not_paper'. The full 6-class MobileNetV2 model described in the technical documentation remains future work (see dissertation status note, 'Next steps').
